# Backend: Midnight Village

Django 5, DRF, Channels, Postgres, managed with `uv`. Start with `just brief server`: the
deploy-safe rules, where each endpoint is built, the files, tests and model slice.

## Commands

<!-- generated by tool/gen_docs.py (commands backend): run it with --fix, never edit by hand -->
```bash
just test-backend [args]   # The backend's tests (and the migration tests when no arguments are given).
just check-backend         # The backend's own quality checks (lint, format check, typecheck, migrations match models): the ...
just fix                   # Run all quality checks and fix what can be fixed
just samples               # Re-record contract_samples/ (repo root) from the real server, after a change to any payload: review ...
just tap-budget            # Re-record tests/perf/tap_budget.json (what each request costs the server at ten seats) after a ...
just server-timing [what]  # Print, per request, timer and socket opening of a whole game at 3, 6 and 10 seats: database round ...
just harness-serve         # Boot the deterministic integration-test harness backend (DEBUG=True, throwaway DB) on ...
```
<!-- end generated -->

Set up with `tool/setup_env.sh <db_name>` (or `just install`): never `uv sync --all-extras`,
never `.env.example` copied as is. `backend/.env` holds your own `DB_NAME` and never
`DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE` (it makes the tests run under dev settings). `docs/dev/environment.md`.

## Deploy-safe changes

The server is live: every push migrates the shared database while the previous build still
serves. The rules, and what checks each: `docs/dev/deploy-vercel.md`, "Deploy-safe changes"
(`just brief server` prints them).

## Rules that have bitten

- **Hidden information in errors.** A refusal never depends on the role: generic messages and
  codes (`bad_request`, `wrong_stage`, ...), never "Seer cannot do that". Targets are plain
  JSON integers; anything else is 400, never coerced.
- **Lock before you check.** Every state change locks the Game row (`select_for_update()`),
  then re-checks phase and stage, then the PlayerRole. Lock order: Game, PlayerRole, Lobby,
  LobbyMember.
- **Side effects after commit.** Socket sends and timer schedule/cancel go through
  `transaction.on_commit`; build payloads inside the transaction. Tests must capture
  on-commit callbacks (`backend/tests/README.md`).
- **Dealt card decides who wakes**, the held card decides who wins.
- **No waits beyond the table's settings.** The night's minimum window and the Doppelganger's
  fixed window are the table's own settings; add no other delay, minimum or assumed default
  length. A stage ends once everyone present has done their part; at night that is
  every phone with a choice (a sleeper is never waited for; a dropped actor holds the window
  through its grace period); window 1 keeps the table's fixed length.
- **Database clock.** Due times, heartbeats and freshness use `Now()`, never an instance clock.
- **WebSocket tests need an authenticated scope**; unauthenticated sockets are rejected
  silently.
- **Throttle rates live in test settings**; without them guest sign-up tests fail with 429s.
- **One process for the memory timer backend** (dev, tests, harness): its timers are threads.
- **Timers in tests**: an autouse fixture makes `timers.schedule` a no-op; `make_night`
  records callbacks you call to run the job; real rows and threads need
  `@pytest.mark.uses_timers` (`backend/tests/README.md`). A test waits on the timer itself
  (`backend/tests/timer_threads.py`), never on a sleep.

## A payload change

`contract_samples/` is recorded from the real API by `backend/tests/contract/scenarios.py`; the
suite fails while the committed files differ. A new endpoint or situation is a
`table.record(...)` line there. After the change: `just samples`, then review every changed
sample: a change the task did not ask for is a bug to fix, not to regenerate. The app's tests
read every sample (`just piece-check` runs them); a body still written by hand
(`frontend/integration_test/helpers/server_bodies.dart`) is this piece's to fix. An open app on
the previous build ignores a key it does not know and fails on a missing one it needs
(`_alwaysSent` in `GameMe.fromJson`): add a key, never rename or drop one in a single push.
Say what the key means in `docs/specs/onuw/api-contract-v2.md`.

## Adding things

- **A role** touches `backend/apps/onuw/engine/roles.py`, `behaviors.py`, `night.py`,
  `win_conditions.py` if it changes the win, `backend/apps/onuw/serializers.py` if it displays
  differently, and tests for each: the type checker will not catch a missed one.
- **A Django app**: `name = "apps.myapp"` in its `AppConfig` (the prefix is easy to forget),
  add it to `INSTALLED_APPS` in `backend/config/settings/base.py`, tests under `backend/tests/<app>/`. A game
  plugs into core through `backend/apps/core/games.py` (`GameHooks`); core imports no game app.
- **Debug harness**: DEBUG-only endpoints (forced deal, `debug-state` oracle,
  `debug-fire-timer`; 403 in production) live in `backend/apps/onuw/debug.py` and
  `debug_views.py`; `backend/tools/game_driver.py` drives a whole game through them
  (`docs/dev/debug-harness/`).
